title: Derived constants, normalized section sources and compactification exchange maps
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring in universe $u+1$ and let all schemes have universe $u$. On the small etale and pro-etale sites use the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. For $t=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$ define $\mathbf A_{T,t}=A_{T,t}[0]$ and $\mathbf P_{i,t}=(i_{t,*}A_{D,t})[0]$ from the constant and supported-constant module sheaves of [def-pur-supported-constant-exchange-maps], for any scheme map $i:D	o T$. Define the inverse-image constant comparisons by the degree-zero derived images of the scalar-preserving constant identifications, and the comparison $q_T:
u_T^*\mathbf A_{T,\mathrm{et}}\cong\mathbf A_{T,\mathrm{proet}}$ by degree-zero derived comparison [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback]. Define $\gamma_i:
u_T^*\mathbf P_{i,\mathrm{et}}	o\mathbf P_{i,\mathrm{proet}}$ as the degree-zero derived image of the supported-constant counit mate, and $ eta_t:v_t^*\mathbf P_{i,t}	o\mathbf P_{i',t}$ as the degree-zero derived image of the canonical supported-constant exchange of [def-pur-supported-constant-base-change-maps] on a chosen Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square].

Suppose additionally that $A$ is finite. Let $h:X	o B$ have a compactification $c=(j,p)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements], and let $s:B\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed section with $h\circ s=1_B$. Put $F_t^c=Rp_{t,*}j_{t,!}$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Let the proper/open interchange be the representative-normalized derived comparison of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]; let direct-image compositors and identity comparisons be the canonical right-derived composites normalized on injective representatives [lem-cbc-etale-derived-direct-image-coherence]. Define $a_c^{\mathrm{et}}:\mathbf A_{B,\mathrm{et}}\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\mathrm{et}}^c\mathbf P_{s,\mathrm{et}}$ as the inverse of the composite $Rp_*j_!s_*A_B\cong Rp_*R(j\circ s)_*A_B\cong R(p\circ j\circ s)_*A_B\cong A_B$, using exact closed direct image and that interchange and those compositors. Write $T_c:
u_B^*F_{\mathrm{et}}^c\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{\mathrm{proet}}^c
u_X^*$ for the specified site comparison [def-sf-compact-support-site-comparison-construction]. Define the source-comparison arrow $b_{c,s}=F_{\mathrm{proet}}^c(\gamma_s)\circ T_c(\mathbf P_{s,\mathrm{et}})$ and define $a_c^{\mathrm{proet}}=b_{c,s}\circ
u_B^*(a_c^{\mathrm{et}})\circ q_B^{-1}$. This last expression defines an arrow, without asserting its invertibility.

For an arbitrary Cartesian square with $h:X	o B$, $g:B'	o B$, $v:X'	o X$ and $h':X'	o B'$, use the pulled-back compactification $c'$. Define the pro-etale compact-support exchange on $D^+$ to be the unique arrow whose fully faithful image in the ambient derived category is the canonical compactification proper/open mate, conjugated by the bounded-below inclusion compatibilities and exact-inverse-image/derived-inverse-image comparisons. The ambient mate first applies proper derived direct-image base change to $j_!M$ and then $Rp′_*$ of the inverse open-extension base-change comparison, with exact inverse image identified with its derived functor. Its etale model is [def-cbc-exchange-map]; for the prescribed positive finite coefficient quotients its ambient pro-etale model is [pur713-def-shriek-exchange]. This is a definition of the actual map for fixed $c$, not an assertion that arbitrary input has etale origin or that exchange is invertible. The formulas for constants, supported constants, their comparison and base-change maps, and the normalized source apply on arbitrary base schemes; no flatness, Noetherian or finite-type condition on $B'$ is imposed.

def proSource [Finite A] {B X : Scheme.{u}} {h : X ⟶ B}
    (c : Compactification h) (s : B ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion s]
    (hs : s ≫ h = 𝟙 B) :
    proConstant A B ⟶
      (ProEtale.rightDerivedLowerShriekOfCompactificationPlus (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) c).obj
        (proSupported A s)
